title: Nuevo Laredo Clinic's Operating Rooms Closed After 74-Year-Old Woman Dies After Cosmetic Surgery
excerpt: Health regulators in Nuevo Laredo closed the operating rooms at the Hospital de Especialidades after a 74-year-old woman died following cosmetic surgery there, finding the clinic's license to perform surgeries was still in process.
content:
Health regulators in Nuevo Laredo have closed the operating rooms at the Hospital de Especialidades, a private clinic, after a 74-year-old woman died there following cosmetic surgery, according to Tamaulipas news reports.

The woman entered the clinic on Monday, Nov. 16, for a cosmetic surgery procedure. After the operation she stayed in the recovery area and was later moved to the outpatient area, where her condition suddenly worsened and she died, according to reports from the state investigators who responded to the clinic.

Hospital staff told the woman's son that she had died of a cardiorespiratory arrest and a fat embolism, a fat clot, according to her family's account to investigators. Her family asked for an autopsy to establish the exact cause of death, and investigators with the Tamaulipas state prosecutor's office and forensic services went to the clinic and ordered the body taken for a necropsy. The investigation remains open, and the exact medical cause of death has not yet been officially confirmed.

On Friday, Nov. 21, the state health-risk protection commission, COEPRIS, closed the clinic's operating rooms. According to the reports, regulators found that the clinic's sanitary license to perform surgeries was still in process, and they also found irregularities in clinical files and medical records.

The local guild of plastic, aesthetic and reconstructive surgeons in Nuevo Laredo, led by Dr. Manuel Sanmiguel, issued a public statement expressing condolences to the woman's family and saying the procedure had been performed by people outside the plastic surgery specialty. The group urged the public to check a doctor's academic credentials and current certifications before undergoing any cosmetic or reconstructive surgery.

The woman's identity has not been made public.

Sources: Lado.mx, Nov. 21, 2026; Central de Noticias Tamaulipas, Nov. 18 and Nov. 19, 2026; Portal Tamaulipas, Nov. 18, 2026.
